_meta.legal_basis: Indian Contract Act 1872 + Trade Marks Act 1999 + Copyright Act 1957 + Competition Act 2002
_meta.notes: Franchise Agreement combines TM/copyright license + operational system + ongoing support + royalty. India has no specific franchise statute (unlike US FTC Franchise Rule). Governed by Contract Act + IP statutes. CCI considerations on territorial exclusivity. Royalty subject to TDS u/s 194J and GST. Cross-border royalty needs FEMA compliance.

title: Franchise Agreement

mandatory_clauses.title: Grant of Franchise
mandatory_clauses.content: Franchisor grants to Franchisee a {{exclusivity}} right and license to operate a {{brand}} franchise outlet within the Territory using the Franchisor's System, Trademarks, and Know-How, subject to the terms of this Agreement.

mandatory_clauses.title: Trademark and IP License
subclauses: Use of TM strictly per brand guidelines
Permitted user registration under S.49 TM Act

mandatory_clauses.title: Initial Franchise Fee
mandatory_clauses.content: Franchisee shall pay an initial franchise fee of INR {{initial_franchise_fee}} on execution, non-refundable, plus applicable GST.

mandatory_clauses.title: Royalty Fee
mandatory_clauses.content: Franchisee shall pay an ongoing royalty of {{royalty_percent}}% of Gross Revenue, payable monthly within 7 days of month-end, plus applicable GST. TDS u/s 194J shall be deducted by Franchisee.

mandatory_clauses.title: Approved Suppliers / Supply Chain
mandatory_clauses.note: Tying arrangements need Competition Act sensitivity - justify on quality/system grounds

mandatory_clauses.title: Non-Compete - In-term and Post-term
mandatory_clauses.note: In-term: enforceable. Post-term: typically 1-2 years within reasonable area - test against S.27 Contract Act and reasonableness.

mandatory_clauses.title: Termination
subclauses: For cause - material breach with cure period

mandatory_clauses.title: Consequences of Termination
subclauses: Return of manuals and confidential information

mandatory_clauses.title: Schedules - Territory, Trademarks, Fee Schedule, Performance Standards

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Franchise Agreement under Indian law. Combine TM license, operating system, training, royalty. Watch Competition Act 2002 for territorial restrictions/tying. India has no franchise-specific statute.
drafting_rules: Franchise = TM license + system + training + ongoing royalty + quality control.
Register the trademark and consider registered user under S.49 TM Act.
Royalty subject to GST (18% on intellectual property licensing). TDS u/s 194J at 10%.
Cross-border franchise: royalty repatriation requires AD Bank reporting per FEMA Current Account Transactions Rules; FDI policy permits royalty up to liberalised limits via automatic route.
Operations Manual is confidential - protect under confidentiality clause.
Quality control is essential for TM license enforceability.
Tying of suppliers - justify on system uniformity/quality, not pure economic exclusion.
Post-term non-compete: limit to 1-2 years and reasonable geographic radius (cite Niranjan Shankar Golikari for reasonableness test).
Termination must include cure period for curable breaches.
De-identification post-termination is critical - prevent passing off.
Stamp duty per state, sometimes ad valorem on franchise fee.
Disclosure: India has no mandatory franchise disclosure document, but good practice to provide FDD-style info.

filing_checklist: Execute on stamp paper per state (ad valorem in some states on initial fee).
Register the TM license / record permitted user under S.49 TM Act with Registrar.
Cross-border: AD Bank reporting; obtain LRS / RBI approvals if required.
Apply for trade licenses, FSSAI (if food), Shops & Establishments registration for franchise outlet.
Maintain Operations Manual as confidential document.
Quarterly TDS return filing on royalty deductions.

validation_rules.check: TM scope, quality control, goodwill clauses present
Post-term restraint geographically and temporally limited
